extracted.intended_audience: fiction writers, screenwriters, students and readers studying narrative structure
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on what a subplot (side story / B story) is, how it relates to the main plot, which characters it usually involves, and how it is distinguished from the main plot. Includes an example of a subplot affecting the main plot.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subplot definition
rubrics_metrics.description: In fiction, a subplot or side story is a strand of the plot that is a supporting side story for any story or for the main plot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subplots serve as supporting strands to the main narrative rather than replacing it. They provide additional storylines that coexist alongside the main plot.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ways subplots connect to the main plot
rubrics_metrics.description: Subplots may connect to main plots, in either time and place or thematic significance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Connections can be temporal (events occur concurrently or at related times), spatial (share locations), or thematic (mirror or contrast themes of the main plot). Such connections can justify including the subplot and give it relevance to the central narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typical characters involved in subplots
rubrics_metrics.description: Subplots often involve supporting characters, those besides the protagonist or antagonist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use secondary or supporting characters to carry subplot arcs, allowing the main characters and main plot to remain central while enriching the world and emotional texture of the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intertwining and influence on main plot
rubrics_metrics.description: Subplots may also intertwine with the main plot at some point in a story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A subplot can directly affect the main plot (introducing obstacles, altering plans, revealing information). Example: in Mr. Robot, a subplot about Angela Moss installing spyware led to The Dark Army withdrawing support for the main hack, forcing the main-plot characters to change strategy. Use intertwining to raise stakes or complicate the main storyline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative scale and impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Subplots are distinguished from the main plot by taking up less of the action, having fewer significant events occur, with less impact on the 'world' of the work, and occurring to less important characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure subplots remain secondary: they should not dominate the narrative, should have fewer major consequences for the overall storyworld, and typically focus on less-central characters. If a subplot eclipses the main plot in scope or consequence, consider promoting it or trimming it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Screenwriting terminology (A story / B story)
rubrics_metrics.description: In screenwriting, a subplot is referred to as a 'B story' while the main plot point can be referred to as the 'A story'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When structuring scripts, label and balance A and B stories consciously: the A story carries the primary dramatic engine; the B story complements it (often thematically) and may provide relief, contrast, or character development.
